name: Grade 9 IIIT: Digital Media Representation
description: STEM launch vocabulary, pixels, resolution, color depth, RGB intensity, image size, samples, sampling rate, sample size, microphones, speakers, compression, quality, and file-size tradeoffs.

words.definition: Problem solving that connects science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
words.example: The STEM project connected media, design, and testing.

words.definition: A way to store, show, or communicate information.
One small picture element in a digital image.
words.example: The mosaic was built pixel by pixel.

words.definition: The number of pixels in an image or display.
words.example: Higher resolution can increase file size.

words.definition: The number of bits used to represent each pixel's color.
words.example: Higher color depth can show more colors.

words.definition: A color model that mixes red, green, and blue.
The strength or amount of a color or signal.
words.example: Higher red intensity made the color warmer.

words.definition: The amount of storage a file uses.
words.example: Higher quality often increased file size.

words.definition: One recorded measurement of sound or data.
words.example: Digital sound is stored as many samples.

words.definition: How many sound samples are recorded per second.
words.example: Higher sampling rate improved sound quality.

words.definition: The number of bits used for each sound sample.
words.example: Sample size affects quality and file size.

words.definition: A device that captures sound input.
words.example: The microphone recorded the audio sample.

words.definition: A device that produces sound output.
words.example: The speaker played the edited sound.

words.definition: Reducing file size by storing data more efficiently.
words.example: Compression made the audio file smaller.

words.definition: How clear or accurate media appears or sounds.
A choice where gaining one benefit may lose another.
words.example: There was a tradeoff between file size and quality.

words.definition: A sound editing tool used to inspect or change audio.
words.example: Students used Audacity to compare sample rates.

words.definition: A table used to record observations and results.
words.example: The evidence table compared sound settings.
